recent_review_examples.scope: The 168-call fixture replays the original tick path without stand-ins for one task exactly at its deadline. It varies task/current priorities, optional event membership, cursor positions, and ready-row counts. Task/event unlink, ready insertion, count/highest-priority updates, next-wakeup sentinel, strict priority comparison, row timeslice, result, and 512-byte/table guards match the fixture oracle. Multi-task due batches, future deadlines, inter-read mutation, and physical tick delivery are not established.

The 48-call fixture replays original tick and next-wakeup code without stand-ins. With both delay lists host-initialized empty, it checks tick wrap, pointer swap, overflow-counter wrap, next-wakeup sentinel, timeslice priority row counts, yield flags, and full backing/table guards. This does not cover due tasks, nonempty old lists, fatal wrap handling, or physical tick behavior.

The 196-byte due-task continuation replays and decodes completely. It compares tick/deadline unsigned, removes the task node and optional event node with sentinel-sensitive cursor repair and count decrements, updates the highest-priority word when needed, and inserts the task into the priority row using the loaded cursor links. Its current-versus-owner priority check is strict: only current priority below the owner sets the yield result; equality does not in this block. The loop rereads the delayed-list global and count. Pointer validity, concurrency, timing, and surrounding scheduler behavior remain unproven.

The 135-case fixture replays original tick processing with no stand-ins. Its suspended cases verify deferred count wrapping without ordinary tick advancement. Normal not-due cases verify tick increments, timeslice row count and priority logic, yield flag, unsigned deadline comparison, return value, and backing/table guards. Host-initialized globals define the scenarios; wrap, due-task handling, fatal behavior, physical ticks, and whole scheduler behavior remain outside scope.

The two mapped ranges replay and decode completely (142 bytes total). A nonzero suspension count increments the deferred-tick word and returns without the ordinary tick update. On the ordinary path the tick increments; wrap checks the current delayed-list count, with a nonempty list entering the mask/fault-store/self-loop path. Empty-list wrap swaps current and overflow list pointers, increments the overflow counter, and calls the next-wakeup helper. The captured tick is compared unsigned against that helper result before branching to the delayed-task body. The tail derives the return flag from priority-row count and the fresh yield word, and restores the documented register set. Tick timing and the mapped body are outside scope.
